facts: Karl Bushby began his round-the-world walking journey in 1998 from Chile.
His absolute rule was no transport of any kind allowed throughout the journey.
He crossed the Darien Gap between South and North America on foot.
He and Dimitri Kieffer crossed the frozen Bering Strait on foot from America to Asia.
His trek across Siberia lasted eleven years with temperatures dropping to minus fifty degrees Celsius.
He crossed the Caspian Sea using a support boat only for rest and sleep alongside Angela Maxwell.
The entire journey spans nearly three decades, 25 countries, and 47,000 kilometers.

script.voiceover_text: Karl Bushby began his journey in 1998 from the southern edge of Chile saying, I'll return home only on foot. After two years he had crossed all of South America and faced his first major obstacle, the Darien Gap. It took six years to cross all of Central and North America and reach the Bering Strait, which separates the two continents. After waiting for the strait to freeze, he and French traveler Dimitri Kieffer became some of the first ever to cross it on foot. His trek across Siberia, where temperatures dropped to minus fifty, stretched over eleven long years. He hit a dead end at the Caspian Sea, so he made one choice, to swim across using a support boat only for rest and sleep. After nearly three decades, twenty five countries, and forty seven thousand kilometers, Karl is now walking across Europe to finally return home.

verdicts.claim: Karl Bushby began his round-the-world walking journey in 1998 from Chile.
verdicts.note: Karl Bushby began his Goliath Expedition on November 1, 1998, from Punta Arenas, Chile.

verdicts.claim: His absolute rule was no transport of any kind allowed throughout the journey.
verdicts.note: Bushby's rule for the Goliath Expedition is that the journey must be continuous and unbroken, meaning no forms of transport are allowed to skip sections.

verdicts.claim: He crossed the Darien Gap between South and North America on foot.
verdicts.note: Bushby and Phil Howard crossed the Darien Gap on foot in 2001.

verdicts.claim: He and Dimitri Kieffer crossed the frozen Bering Strait on foot from America to Asia.
verdicts.note: Bushby and Dimitri Kieffer crossed the frozen Bering Strait from Alaska (America) to Siberia (Asia) on foot in 2006.

verdicts.claim: His trek across Siberia lasted eleven years with temperatures dropping to minus fifty degrees Celsius.
verdicts.note: Due to visa issues, bureaucratic delays, and walking distance, his trek through Russia/Siberia spanned many years, and winter temperatures in Siberia frequently drop below -50°C.

verdicts.claim: He crossed the Caspian Sea using a support boat only for rest and sleep alongside Angela Maxwell.
verdicts.note: Bushby and Angela Maxwell crossed the Caspian Sea in 2019 using a rowing boat, swimming/walking sections where possible and using the boat for support.

verdicts.claim: The entire journey spans nearly three decades, 25 countries, and 47,000 kilometers.
verdicts.note: The Goliath Expedition is planned to cover roughly 36,000 to 57,000 km across 25+ countries over multiple decades (started in 1998, ongoing).
